n41f5d2b79f7.s:
Consider the following statements about the Hindu-Muslim unity of 1857:
1. It was later cited against the two-nation theory.
2. It was later cited in support of the Doctrine of Lapse.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n41f5d2b79f7.x: The Hindu-Muslim unity of the revolt was later cited against the two-nation theory; it had nothing to do with the Doctrine of Lapse.

n1f46901aa63.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched (centre – date the rising began, 1857)?
n1f46901aa63.x: The rising at Kanpur began on 5 June 1857, not 11 May; 11 May is the date the rebels reached Delhi.

n987adf86352.s: Which of the following pairs (historian – view of 1857) is correctly matched?
o: R.C. Majumdar – First War of Independence
Eric Stokes – Many local peasant and elite risings
V.D. Savarkar – A mere sepoy mutiny
n987adf86352.x: Eric Stokes, using local agrarian studies, saw the revolt as many peasant and elite risings, not one centrally directed movement.

nda817aa3618.s: The Revolt of 1857 was confined largely to which part of India, while most of India remained neutral?
nda817aa3618.x: The revolt did not spread evenly; it was largely confined to North India, which is one limit of calling it the First War of Independence.

n6bb6651c190.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Hindu-Muslim relations in the Revolt of 1857?
o: Bahadur Shah II was accepted by both Hindu and Muslim rebels
The greased cartridges offended both Hindus and Muslims
The British responded with a policy of divide and rule
The British responded by transferring authority to the Indian National Congress
n6bb6651c190.x: The British answered Hindu-Muslim cooperation with divide and rule; there was no transfer of authority to the Congress.

new.s: Mangal Pandey, who attacked Lt Baugh at Barrackpore, belonged to the:
new.x: Mangal Pandey of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry attacked Lt Baugh at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857; the 3rd Cavalry rose later at Meerut.

new.s: How many sepoys of the 3rd Cavalry were sentenced at Meerut on 9 May 1857 for refusing the cartridges?
new.x: On 9 May 1857, 85 sepoys of the 3rd (Bengal Light) Cavalry at Meerut were sentenced to 10 years for refusing the cartridges.

new.s: Where did the Revolt of 1857 really begin on 10 May 1857?
new.x: Barrackpore saw the first outbreak (29 March), but the revolt really began at Meerut on 10 May 1857.

new.s: Mangal Pandey was hanged on:
new.x: Mangal Pandey was hanged on 8 April 1857 and the 34th BNI was disbanded; 29 March was the day of his attack.

new.s: Which were the symbols of the Revolt of 1857?
new.x: The lotus and the chapati were the symbols of the Revolt of 1857.

new.s: The rising at Kanpur, where Nana Saheb was proclaimed Peshwa, began on:
new.x: Nana Saheb was proclaimed Peshwa at Kanpur on 5 June 1857, the day the rising there began; Lucknow rose fully on 4 June.

new.s: The rising at Jhansi began in:
new.x: The rising at Jhansi began in June 1857, not on 11 May, which was the day the rebels reached Delhi.

new.s: Which of the following areas rose in October 1857?
new.x: The Kolhapur area rose in October 1857; Gwalior rose in June and Indore in July 1857.

new.s: Who was the real military leader of the rebels at Delhi in 1857?
new.x: Bahadur Shah II was only the nominal leader at Delhi; General Bakht Khan was the real military leader.

new.s: General Bakht Khan led a 'Court of Soldiers' of how many members at Delhi?
new.x: Bakht Khan, who reached Delhi from Bareilly on 3 July 1857, led a 10-member 'Court of Soldiers'.

new.s: The army of Khan Bahadur Khan at Bareilly numbered about:
new.x: Khan Bahadur Khan of Bareilly proclaimed himself Nawab Nizam and had an army of about 40,000.

new.s: Thakur Kushal Singh, who beat the British-Jodhpur army in 1857, led the revolt at:
new.x: Thakur Kushal Singh of Auwa in Rajputana beat the British-Jodhpur army in 1857.

new.s: Who led the revolt of 1857 in Assam?
new.x: Maniram Dewan (Dutt) led the revolt of 1857 in Assam.

new.s: Jhalkari Bai, the lookalike of Rani Lakshmibai, fought in 1857 at:
new.x: Jhalkari Bai, Lakshmibai's lookalike, commanded the women's wing at Jhansi.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (local leader – centre) is correctly matched?
new.x: Azizun was active at Kanpur; Uda Devi fought at Lucknow, Jhalkari Bai at Jhansi and Shah Mal at Baraut.

new.s: Tantia Tope, commander-in-chief of Nana Saheb, was originally named:
new.x: Tantia Tope, Nana Saheb's commander-in-chief, was originally named Ramachandra Pandurang.

new.s: W.H. Russell recorded the revolt and British revenge in:
new.x: W.H. Russell, correspondent of The Times, reported the revolt and British revenge in 'My Diary in India'.

new.s: The rebels at Delhi proclaimed Bahadur Shah II as:
new.x: The rebels at Delhi proclaimed Bahadur Shah II 'Shahenshah-e-Hindustan'; Nawab Nizam was the title of Khan Bahadur Khan.

new.s: The pension of Bahadur Shah Zafar was:
new.x: Bahadur Shah Zafar's pension was one lakh rupees a month (Rs 99,000 in Delhi and Rs 1,000 in Lucknow).

new.s: Who recaptured Jhansi in April 1858?
new.x: Hugh Rose recaptured Jhansi in April 1858 and Gwalior in June 1858.

new.s: Kanpur was first recaptured on 16 July 1857 by:
new.x: Henry Havelock first recaptured Kanpur on 16 July 1857; Colin Campbell retook it in December 1857.

new.s: Where was Tantia Tope hanged on 18 April 1859?
new.x: Tantia Tope was betrayed, captured and hanged at Shivpuri on 18 April 1859, the last major leader executed.

new.s: Kunwar Singh died on 26 April 1858 at:
new.x: Kunwar Singh was wounded crossing the Ganga and died at Jagdishpur on 26 April 1858.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the fate of rebel leaders:
1. Nana Saheb escaped to Nepal.
2. Begum Hazrat Mahal escaped to Nepal.
3. Tantia Tope escaped to Nepal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Nana Saheb and Begum Hazrat Mahal escaped to Nepal; Tantia Tope was captured and executed in 1859.

new.s: In which pair of states did the troops rebel in 1857 while the rulers stayed loyal?
new.x: At Tonk and Bhopal the troops rebelled but the rulers stayed loyal; Jaipur and Chittor were not centres of the revolt.

new.s: Which Rajputana centre saw a sepoy rising in May 1857?
new.x: Nasirabad saw a sepoy rising in May 1857; the rising at Neemuch came in June 1857.

new.s: Turrebaz Khan led the attack on the British Residency at Hyderabad on:
new.x: Turrebaz Khan, with Maulvi Allauddin, attacked the Hyderabad Residency from the Mecca Masjid on 17 July 1857.

new.s: Sheikh Peer Shah, imprisoned for secret contact with sepoys in 1857, was from:
new.x: Sheikh Peer Shah of Cuddapah (Rayalaseema) had secret contact with the Cuddapah sepoys and was imprisoned.

new.s: Who was imprisoned in Golconda before Turrebaz Khan's attack on the Hyderabad Residency?
new.x: Mubariz-ud-Daula was imprisoned in Golconda before Turrebaz Khan's attack; Nizam Afzal-ud-Daula stayed pro-British.

new.s: Under the Government of India Act 1858, the Governor-General was given the title of:
new.x: The Government of India Act 1858 gave power to the Crown, created a Secretary of State and made the Governor-General the Viceroy.

new.s: The largest number of soldiers in the Revolt of 1857 came from:
new.x: The largest number of soldiers in the revolt, over 75,000 sepoys, came from Oudh.

new.s: Who became Commander-in-Chief in 1857 after General Anson died?
new.x: Sir Colin Campbell became Commander-in-Chief after General Anson died in 1857.

new.s: Lord Canning formally declared peace after the revolt on:
new.x: Lord Canning declared peace on 8 July 1858; 1 November 1858 was the date of the Queen's Proclamation.

new.s: Sir Colin Campbell was later known as:
new.x: Sir Colin Campbell, the Commander-in-Chief who retook Lucknow, was later Lord Clyde.

new.s: Who shot the sons of Bahadur Shah II after the fall of Delhi?
new.x: After Delhi fell, Hodson captured Bahadur Shah II and shot his sons, ending the Mughal line.

new.s: Nagpur (Bhonsle) had no ruler to join the revolt because it had been annexed in:
new.x: Nagpur (Bhonsle) had already been annexed in 1854, so there was no ruler to join the revolt.

new.s: Which presidency armies remained loyal to the British in 1857?
new.x: The revolt was chiefly of the Bengal Army; the Madras and Bombay armies stayed loyal.

new.s: Which group acted as 'breakwaters' in 1857 to protect its class interests?
new.x: Big zamindars and moneylenders acted as 'breakwaters' to protect their class interests.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Indian classes during the Revolt of 1857?
o: The educated middle class remained neutral
The educated middle class led the rising at Delhi
Big zamindars and moneylenders protected their class interests
Merchants and the urban elite gave no support
new.x: The educated middle class remained neutral, seeing the revolt as a backward-looking feudal reaction; it did not lead any rising.

new.s: Who suppressed the revolt of Kunwar Singh in Bihar?
new.x: William Taylor suppressed the revolt of Kunwar Singh in Bihar; Colonel Neill retook Allahabad and Banaras.

new.s: Which British officer was killed in the assault on Delhi in 1857?
new.x: John Nicholson was killed leading the assault on Delhi; Lawrence, Neill and Havelock fell at Lucknow.

new.s: Rani Avantibai Lodhi of Ramgarh defeated Waddington in 1857 at:
new.x: Rani Avantibai Lodhi of Ramgarh beat Waddington at Kheri near Mandla and died in 1858.

new.s: Jhansi, the state of Rani Lakshmibai, had lapsed to the British in:
new.x: Jhansi lapsed to the British in 1854; Rani Lakshmibai was the widow of Gangadhar Rao.

new.s: British troops returning from which war strengthened the suppression of 1857?
new.x: Troops returning from the Crimea and experienced generals strengthened the British against the rebels.

new.s: Rebel unity in Awadh was weakened by quarrels between the Begum of Awadh and:
new.x: Quarrels such as that between the Begum of Awadh and Maulvi Ahmadullah weakened rebel unity.

new.s: T.R. Holmes described the Revolt of 1857 as a conflict between:
new.x: T.R. Holmes saw the revolt as a conflict of civilisation against barbarism.

new.s: Who asked in the House of Commons in 1857, 'Is it a military mutiny, or is it a national revolt?'
new.x: Benjamin Disraeli asked in the Commons on 27 July 1857, 'Is it a military mutiny, or is it a national revolt?'

new.s: Karl Marx called the revolt 'in truth a national revolt' in the:
new.x: Karl Marx wrote in the New-York Tribune (1857) that what John Bull called a mutiny was in truth a national revolt.

new.s: Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind (1859) was written by:
new.x: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind in 1859; Mirza Ghalib was the poet who witnessed the revolt.

new.s: '1857: The Great Rebellion' was written by:
new.x: '1857: The Great Rebellion' was written by Ashok Mehta.

new.s: 'Awadh in Revolt' was written by:
new.x: 'Awadh in Revolt' was written by Rudrangshu Mukherjee.

new.s: Rudrangshu Mukherjee studied the resistance of peasants and taluqdars in:
new.x: Rudrangshu Mukherjee studied peasant and taluqdar resistance in Awadh.

new.s: Nehru called the Revolt of 1857 essentially a feudal rising in:
new.x: Nehru called the revolt essentially a feudal rising in The Discovery of India.

new.s: The 'mutiny or revolt' debate is also applied to the RIN revolt that began on HMIS Talwar in:
new.x: The same 'mutiny or revolt?' debate applies to the RIN revolt that began on HMIS Talwar on 18 February 1946.

new.s: Which groups joined the Revolt of 1857 in Awadh and western UP?
o: Bengal zamindars and the urban elite
new.x: Awadh taluqdars, peasants and artisans joined the revolt in Awadh and western UP, while the big zamindars of Bengal stayed loyal.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about labels for the Revolt of 1857:
1. British historians called it the Sepoy Mutiny.
2. V.D. Savarkar called it the First War of Independence.
3. The feudal-reaction view stresses the role of the educated middle class.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: British historians called it the Sepoy Mutiny and Savarkar the First War of Independence; the feudal-reaction view stresses dispossessed princes and taluqdars, not the educated class.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the centenary histories of 1857:
1. S.N. Sen's 'Eighteen Fifty-Seven' was government-commissioned.
2. R.C. Majumdar's 'The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857' was an independent work.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Sen wrote the official, government-commissioned history in 1957; Majumdar parted with the official project and wrote independently.
